strategy.summary: TestForge's axe scan found / and /contact free of violations with no axe check guarding them. Add a Playwright axe check (via @axe-core/playwright, already a devDependency) for each page in its existing spec file, failing on any violation rated minor or worse and naming each rule and its elements. No new violations were reported, so no defects are recorded; the known color-contrast on /about and image-alt on /cart are left alone.
inScope: A shared helper in tests/support/axe.js that filters violations to minor-or-worse impacts and formats rule ids and element targets
outOfScope: Known violations color-contrast on /about and image-alt on /cart (already reported, issues open)
Keyboard and screen-reader testing, which axe can't prove
assumptions: The app is served by the existing playwright.config.js webServer (node server.js on port 4174); the real server runs, nothing is faked.

The axe check is added as a new test beside the existing one in each page's spec file (each opens the page with a literal path), so the existing tests stay unchanged and each test checks one behaviour.
The scan runs all axe rules (no withTags filter) and fails on every impact from minor up, matching what the TestForge scan reported, rather than the skill's critical/serious default.

candidates.text: The axe_checks publish gate only counts a page as guarded when the spec file itself calls `new AxeBuilder({ page }).analyze()` after a literal `page.goto('/path')`. Wrapping the AxeBuilder call in a helper module is not detected. Keep analyze() in the spec and put only the impact filtering in tests/support/axe.js (guardedViolations).
candidates.evidence: self_check reported '/ passed the scan but no changed e2e test checks it with axe' while AxeBuilder lived in tests/support/axe.js; ready once analyze() moved into the specs.
